project.name: Corvane R2R eval
project.problemStatement: Record-to-report at Corvane Advisory Group is a spreadsheet-driven close across four legal entities, with manual intercompany matching, Excel revenue recognition and consolidation, manual bank reconciliations and a close that takes 11 working days.

opening: We are Corvane Advisory Group (fictional), a professional services group with about £280 million revenue, 1,900 staff and four legal entities in the UK, Ireland, the Netherlands and Singapore. We report under IFRS in pounds sterling and our month-end close takes 11 working days. Each entity keeps its books in a separate cloud accounting package, timesheets come from TimeTrack, and everything else is Excel: intercompany recharges are agreed by email and matrix, revenue on fixed-fee projects is recognised from a percentage-of-completion spreadsheet, accruals are collected by email, and group consolidation is a workbook with links to each entity's trial balance. Bank accounts at five banks are reconciled by hand. Our auditors have raised findings on intercompany differences and on the audit trail behind manual journals. We want to move to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition within ten months and shorten the close.

catalog.process_owner: The Group Financial Controller owns the close and consolidation, entity finance managers own their ledgers and bank reconciliations, and the Head of Revenue Accounting owns revenue recognition.
catalog.scope_boundary: The process starts when subledger and timesheet data are final for the month and ends when the consolidated management and statutory reporting pack is signed off. It covers all four legal entities, including intercompany, fixed assets, accruals, bank reconciliation and revenue recognition, and excludes payroll and tax computation.
catalog.current_trigger: The Group Financial Controller publishes the close calendar and each entity finance manager starts the close when timesheets are locked on the last working day.
catalog.current_systems: We use four separate cloud accounting packages, TimeTrack for timesheets, Excel for revenue recognition, intercompany, accruals and consolidation, five bank portals, and email for approvals. Journals move between systems as CSV files, so every figure is re-keyed or uploaded.
catalog.current_rules: Manual journals above £50,000 need the entity finance manager's approval by email. Fixed-fee revenue is recognised over time on cost-to-cost progress, reviewed by the Head of Revenue Accounting. Intercompany recharges are agreed between entities by the 3rd working day.
catalog.current_exceptions: Late timesheets are posted into the following month. Intercompany balances that do not agree are explained in a spreadsheet and often carried forward. Journals posted after the books close are re-opened by emailing the accounting package administrator.
catalog.current_financial: Each entity reports in its local currency and is revalued manually at month-end rates, with translation to pounds sterling in the consolidation workbook. Intercompany eliminations and goodwill adjustments are manual journals. There is no single chart of accounts, so a mapping table translates entity accounts to group accounts.
catalog.desired_outcome: Close in 4 working days, intercompany differences cleared automatically with fewer than 1% unmatched items at close, 90% of bank statement lines reconciled automatically, and one consolidated ledger and reporting pack without Excel.
catalog.desired_controls: We need a single group chart of accounts, automated intercompany matching and elimination, IFRS 15 revenue recognition with an audit trail, approval and a full audit trail on manual journals, bank reconciliation with automatic matching, and a close task list with sign-off per entity. TimeTrack stays as the timesheet system and must be integrated, and we prefer standard SAP over custom development.
catalog.process_overview: The process runs in these stages. Lock timesheets and billing data: Resource managers chase consultants to submit timesheets, lock the period in TimeTrack and send a CSV of hours and rates to finance. Post subledger and manual journals: Each entity accountant posts payables, receivables, payroll and manual journals in the local package. Agree intercompany recharges: The group accountant builds a recharge matrix for management fees and shared staff time, emails each entity to confirm it and asks each entity to post its half in its own package. Recognise revenue under IFRS 15: The revenue accountant calculates cost-to-cost progress for each fixed-fee project in Excel, determines revenue earned, compares it with amounts billed and keys a contract asset or contract liability journal. Collect accruals and prepayments: Accountants email budget holders for uninvoiced costs, collect replies in Excel, book accruals and reverse them the next month. Depreciate fixed assets: The accountant maintains an asset register in Excel per entity, calculates monthly depreciation under IFRS rules and posts a summary journal. Reconcile bank accounts: The accountant downloads statements from five banks, compares each line with the ledger in Excel and posts differences. Revalue foreign currency balances: The accountant gets rates from a treasury email, computes unrealised gains and losses on foreign currency payables, receivables and bank balances in Excel and sends journals to each entity to post. Reconcile and eliminate intercompany: The accountant exports intercompany balances from each package, compares counterparty balances in Excel and lists the differences. Consolidate and report: The controller maps entity accounts to group accounts, translates results to pounds sterling, adds adjustments and produces the management and statutory packs. Sign off and lock the period: The controller emails each entity finance manager to lock the period, files the reconciliations in a shared folder and keeps the close checklist in Excel.
catalog.operating_scale: We have about £280 million revenue, 1,900 staff and four legal entities, and our bank accounts at five banks produce a large volume of statement lines every month.
catalog.legal_entities: There are four legal entities: Corvane Advisory UK, Ireland, the Netherlands and Singapore, each keeping its books in a separate package.
catalog.target_org_units: We plan company codes 3000 for the UK, 3100 for Ireland, 3200 for the Netherlands and 3300 for Singapore.
catalog.modules_in_scope: The scope covers finance, controlling, asset accounting, project systems and treasury and risk management.
catalog.retained_systems: TimeTrack stays as the timesheet system and must be integrated with SAP. The four local accounting packages and the Excel workbooks are replaced.
catalog.external_parties: We deal with five banks, our external auditors, and the tax and statutory filing authorities in the UK, Ireland, the Netherlands and Singapore.
catalog.kpi_baselines: Today the month-end close takes 11 working days, intercompany balances differ by about 2% at close, and about 70% of bank statement lines are matched by hand.
catalog.kpi_targets: A close in 4 working days, fewer than 1% unmatched intercompany items at close, and 90% of bank statement lines reconciled automatically.
catalog.timeline: We want to be live on SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition within ten months.
catalog.constraints: We prefer standard SAP over custom development. TimeTrack is kept and integrated, and the four local accounting packages are retired.
catalog.localization_compliance: We report under IFRS in pounds sterling and need IFRS 15 revenue recognition with an audit trail, plus the statutory reporting of each country.
catalog.approval_rules: Manual journals above £50,000 need the entity finance manager's approval by email today, and we want approval with a full audit trail inside the system.
catalog.required_outputs: We need a consolidated management and statutory reporting pack, an intercompany reconciliation report, bank reconciliation reports and a close task list with sign-off per entity.

steps.name: Lock timesheets and billing data
steps.trigger: The last working day of the month.
steps.description: Resource managers chase consultants to submit timesheets, lock the period in TimeTrack and send a CSV of hours and rates to finance. Late timesheets are left for the next month.
steps.inputs: Timesheet entries; project rate cards; leave records
steps.outputs: Locked timesheet CSV by project and entity
steps.controls: Resource managers approve timesheets before the lock
steps.exceptions: Timesheets submitted after the lock are carried into the next month and distort project margins.

steps.name: Post subledger and manual journals
steps.trigger: The month-end calendar opens the period for journals.
steps.description: Each entity accountant posts payables, receivables, payroll and manual journals in the local package. Manual journals are prepared in Excel and uploaded as CSV with approval by email.
steps.inputs: Supplier and customer invoices; payroll journal; journal workbook
steps.outputs: Posted entity ledger; manual journal list
steps.controls: The entity finance manager approves manual journals above £50,000 by email
steps.exceptions: Journals posted after the period is closed require an administrator to re-open the books.

steps.name: Agree intercompany recharges
steps.trigger: Timesheet and cost data are final for the month.
steps.description: The group accountant builds a recharge matrix for management fees and shared staff time, emails each entity to confirm it and asks each entity to post its half in its own package. Entities rarely post on the same day.
steps.inputs: Timesheet CSV; shared cost lists; recharge policy
steps.outputs: Agreed recharge matrix; intercompany invoices keyed per entity
steps.controls: Both entity finance managers confirm the amount by email
steps.exceptions: Disagreements on amounts or currencies are resolved by phone, and unmatched balances are carried forward.

steps.name: Recognise revenue under IFRS 15
steps.trigger: Project cost and timesheet data are final.
steps.description: The revenue accountant calculates cost-to-cost progress for each fixed-fee project in Excel, determines revenue earned, compares it with amounts billed and keys a contract asset or contract liability journal. Multi-element contracts are split by hand.
steps.inputs: Contract terms; project costs to date; estimated cost to complete; billing schedule
steps.controls: The Head of Revenue Accounting reviews projects above £250,000
steps.exceptions: Contract modifications and changes in estimated cost to complete are adjusted manually and sometimes missed.

steps.name: Collect accruals and prepayments
steps.trigger: The close calendar reaches accruals day.
steps.description: Accountants email budget holders for uninvoiced costs, collect replies in Excel, book accruals and reverse them the next month. Recurring prepayments are amortised from a schedule.
steps.inputs: Budget holder replies; open orders; prepayment schedule
steps.controls: Journals above £50,000 are approved by the entity finance manager
steps.exceptions: Late replies mean accruals are estimated from last month, and reversals are sometimes forgotten.

steps.name: Depreciate fixed assets
steps.trigger: The period is open for asset postings.
steps.description: The accountant maintains an asset register in Excel per entity, calculates monthly depreciation under IFRS rules and posts a summary journal. Disposals and additions are added by hand.
steps.inputs: Asset register; capital invoices; disposal forms
steps.controls: The register is reconciled to the general ledger quarterly
steps.exceptions: Assets bought late in the month are depreciated from the wrong date and corrected in the next close.

steps.name: Reconcile bank accounts
steps.trigger: Bank statements are available after month end.
steps.description: The accountant downloads statements from five banks, compares each line with the ledger in Excel and posts differences. Around 70% of lines are matched by hand each month.
steps.inputs: Bank statements; ledger bank account; payment lists
steps.controls: The entity finance manager signs the reconciliation
steps.exceptions: Unidentified receipts stay in a suspense account and are cleared the following month.

steps.name: Revalue foreign currency balances
steps.description: The accountant gets rates from a treasury email, computes unrealised gains and losses on foreign currency payables, receivables and bank balances in Excel and sends journals to each entity to post.
steps.inputs: Month-end rates; open foreign currency balances
steps.controls: The Group Financial Controller reviews the total gain or loss
steps.exceptions: A wrong rate table is usually found after consolidation and the journals are reversed and re-posted.

steps.name: Reconcile and eliminate intercompany
steps.trigger: All entities have posted their recharges and revaluations.
steps.description: The accountant exports intercompany balances from each package, compares counterparty balances in Excel and lists the differences. Eliminating journals are keyed in the workbook. Differences of 2% of balances are common at close.
steps.inputs: Entity trial balances; intercompany balance extracts
steps.controls: The Group Financial Controller reviews unresolved differences
steps.exceptions: Differences that cannot be explained are parked in a group suspense line and carried forward.

steps.name: Consolidate and report
steps.description: The controller maps entity accounts to group accounts, translates results to pounds sterling, adds adjustments and produces the management and statutory packs. Segment and project profitability are rebuilt in Excel.
steps.inputs: Entity trial balances; mapping table; exchange rates; adjustment journals
steps.outputs: Consolidated trial balance; management pack; statutory pack
steps.controls: The CFO signs off the packs
steps.exceptions: Late entity adjustments force a rework of the whole workbook and the close takes 11 working days.

steps.name: Sign off and lock the period
steps.description: The controller emails each entity finance manager to lock the period, files the reconciliations in a shared folder and keeps the close checklist in Excel. There is no central record of who approved which journal.
steps.inputs: CFO approval; close checklist; reconciliation files
steps.outputs: Locked periods; close checklist; audit file
steps.controls: Entity finance managers confirm the lock by email
steps.exceptions: Post-close adjustments are posted into the next month and the audit trail is rebuilt from emails.

requirements.statement: TimeTrack stays as the timesheet system and must be integrated with SAP for project hours and billing, not replaced.
Manual journals are approved by email with no central audit trail, which has led to audit findings.
A single group chart of accounts must replace the four local charts and the mapping table.
Intercompany recharges are agreed by email and posted separately by each entity, so counterparty balances differ by about 2% at close.
Intercompany differences must be cleared automatically with fewer than 1% unmatched items at close.
IFRS 15 revenue on fixed-fee projects is calculated in Excel, so contract modifications and estimate changes are missed and there is no audit trail.
Accruals are collected by email, estimated from last month when replies are late, and reversals are sometimes forgotten.
The asset register is an Excel file, so late additions are depreciated from the wrong date.
About 70% of bank statement lines are matched by hand across five banks, and unidentified receipts sit in suspense.
At least 90% of bank statement lines must be reconciled automatically.
Foreign currency revaluation is calculated in Excel and journals are sent to each entity, so a wrong rate is found only after consolidation.
Consolidation is a linked Excel workbook, so any late entity adjustment forces rework.
The month-end close must take 4 working days, down from 11, with a task list and sign-off per entity.
